source_title: Tom Francis and Ray Nicholson Bonded During ‘The Mosquito Bowl’ Training (Exclusive) - People.com
source_excerpt:
The actors tell PEOPLE how a month of football practice and military boot camp helped them forge an instant bond before filming their new World War II drama
Tommy McArdle is a Writer-Reporter on the Movies team at PEOPLE. He joined the brand in 2022.
The Mosquito Bowl stars Tom Francis and Ray Nicholson tell PEOPLE how they bonded while undergoing football and military training to prepare for their roles in the new World War II drama
The actors star alongside Nicholas Galitzine and Bill Skarsgård in the film, which follows four former college football stars who enlist in the U.S. Marine Corps during World War II.
Based on the 2022 nonfiction book of the same name, The Mosquito Bowl hits theaters Oct. 30 before streaming on Netflix Nov. 25.
Tom Francis and Ray Nicholson quickly forged a friendship on the football field — and during military training drills — while preparing for their new movie.
Francis, 27, and Nicholson, 34, star alongside Nicholas Galitzine and Bill Skarsgård in The Mosquito Bowl , which follows four former college football players who enlist in the U.S. Marine Corps during World War II.
Inspired by the real-life stories of athletes-turned-soldiers John McLaughry (Galitzine, 31), Bob Bauman (Skarsgård, 36), Tony Butkovich (Nicholson) and David Schreiner (Francis), the film brought its stars to Australia a month before filming began for football practice and a military-style boot camp. As Francis and Nicholson tell PEOPLE, the experience helped them build a bond long before cameras started rolling.
“We basically spent three or four hours in the morning doing football training, and then three or four hours in the afternoon doing military training,” Francis, the Tony Award -nominated actor, says. “I think it was needed. There’s two Brits and Swede and then one American coming into an American football-war movie, so the football side of it was definitely needed. But it was also just great in terms of figuring out who we were and how we interact with each other, and building that brotherhood bond and understanding what makes each other tick.”
Francis recalls a recent conversation with Nicholson in which they reflected on how their time training together helped ease their nerves once filming began.
“We had a month to really get to know each other. We loved each other straight away. All of us, we were like, ‘This is gonna be the best thing ever,’” he says.
With a hearty laugh, Francis then quotes Will Ferrell ‘s memorable line from the 2008 comedy Step Brothers to describe their instant connection: “We instantly just became, ‘ Did we just become best friends? ‘”
“It just all happened. And then it just means that when you turn up on day one, that’s not a thing that you’re thinking about,” he adds. “That’s an anxiety that’s gone. It was a really, really invaluable month that we had. It was a luxury.”
The Mosquito Bowl follows McLaughry, Bauman, Butkovich and Schreiner from college football fields in the U.S. in the early 1940s to the brutal fighting in the Pacific Theater during World War II. Based on Buzz Bissinger’s 2022 nonfiction book of the same name , the film builds toward a football game organized on Christmas Day 1944 by Marines stationed on the island of Guadalcanal. Many of the men had been college athletes before enlisting, and the game offered a brief respite from the horrors of war.
Nicholson grew up playing football in Los Angeles, while Francis was a relative newcomer to the sport.
“We would hit bags, and a lot of it is just getting used to running with the weight of a helmet and shoulder pads on. So that was definitely more physically demanding,” Nicholson says of the training the cast went through, which took place on a cricket pitch in Australia. “It was an hour for lunch and then another three hours of military. I would find myself falling asleep in the line and [military advisor James Dever] would chew me out and make me do pushups and run. It hit both levels beautifully, but it was also a weird thing for the characters. I had never done something where you establish character relationships on a football field.”

He adds that the fun of “playing football with your boys” was balanced by more intense military training exercises designed to simulate the realities of combat during World War II.
“When we were shooting we had this excitement and this intensity playing football, and then a different kind of intensity for the war stuff. Once we got back to football, we were like, ‘Oh my God. We’re so happy.’ You can only imagine what these guys must have actually felt,” Nicholson says. “I don’t know if it was intentional, but it really worked beautifully.”
The Mosquito Bowl is in theaters Oct. 30. The movie begins streaming on Netflix Nov. 25.
